<description>
In this design there is a new GHA job merged into the main repo that adds check runs to each PR on whether they have a silent merge conflict or not.

The idea is that we have a job that pretty much runs 24/7 triggered every 6 hours or so and set to run for 5.5 hours, it could be set to run on a GHA runner rather than a Cirrus runner. Obviously running on a Cirrus runner (or even multiple runners) would dramatically speed up how many PRs can be checked for silent merge conflicts.

The job uses the Github checks API to add a passing or failing test run to each PR directly. The silent merge check job itself should always pass, it writes pass or fail checks to the PRs.

It will look through all open PRs and discard anything that has a git merge failure or a failing test with the thinking that there is no point checking something that can't be merged anyway. Then it will select PRs that have not had a silent merge check and one by one pull the merge branch of the PR and the full CI job "Previous releases" on that branch.

When all PRs have been checked it will then re-check a PR that was checked the longest time ago.
</description>

This is very awkward to test so here is a starting point prompt for your AI to set up a test in your fork. Hope this is helpful:

  Prompt to test this on a fork

Test the silent-merge workflow from this branch on my fork of bitcoin/bitcoin.
  The workflow only runs from the fork's default branch, which must be named master, because the script merges each pull request onto refs/heads/master. If replacing that branch would destroy anything, stop and
  ask first. On top of this branch, add one commit that exists only on the fork:
  - In .github/workflows/silent-merge-check.yml, remove the `if: github.repository == 'bitcoin/bitcoin'` guard from the verify-prs job.
  - At the top of skip_reason() in .github/silent-merge-test.py, return None immediately. Mark that commit DELETE ME. The fixtures will have no passing check runs, so without this the script skips them. Push
  that commit only to the fork's master.
  If the "Silent Merge Periodic Check" workflow is disabled, enable it. Pushing branches will start the normal Bitcoin CI. Cancel those runs so they do not occupy runners. Leave the silent-merge run going.
  From that master, before merging anything, open three pull requests of one commit each:
  1. Cause. In TrimString() in src/util/string.h, return an empty string when the input is exactly "silent_merge".
  2. Victim. In util_TrimString in src/test/util_tests.cpp, add BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(TrimString("silent_merge"), "silent_merge"). This passes on its own and fails once the cause is on master.
  3. Always-pass. In the same test, add BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(TrimString("silent_merge9"), "silent_merge9").
  Dispatch silent-merge-check.yml and wait for it. The first run should test all three, all three should pass, and each head should get a "Periodic silent merge check" check run. The workflow run stays green.
  Then merge only the cause pull request, cancel the normal CI that the merge starts, and dispatch the workflow again. The victim should fail in util_TrimString because TrimString("silent_merge") is empty. The
  always-pass pull request should pass. The workflow run itself should still be green, with the failure recorded on the victim's check run.
  Report both run URLs and the check conclusions. Do not change the script based on a guess about what might fail. The DELETE ME commit stays on the fork.
